title: Lawa'ih
shelf_note: Jami's Lawa'ih, a core Persian Sufi treatise (wahdat al-wujud), in the 1906 Royal Asiatic Society facsimile with Whinfield/Qazvini English apparatus.
structure_note: Mixed volume: a lithographed Persian facsimile followed by the 1906 English typeset matter. The English part is scanned in reverse order: the title page sits at page 123 of 124 and Appendix I (printed p. 59) at page 65. The 34 printed-number backsteps come from that reversal (I6), not from misread numerals. 18 of 124 pages have no OCR and 27 are untranslated. The English pages are 'translated' as English echoes of themselves, which does no harm. Whinfield's own 1906 English translation is in the volume, but a reader of the Persian pages gets only the AI translation.

book_verdict: A core Sufi text in a public-domain 1906 edition. The Persian OCR misreads key doctrinal lines (the 'one true Existent' sentence and the 'keep the levels or be a heretic' quatrain), and the English renders those misreads fluently, with a reversed meaning in one place. The English back matter is in reverse order.
reader_summary: This is Jami's Lawa'ih in a lithographed Persian facsimile, with the 1906 Royal Asiatic Society English matter at the back. The transcription is of the right text and mostly sound in the prose, but it garbles verses and several doctrinal key sentences, and the English then states those garbles as Jami's meaning. A scholar should read the English against Whinfield's translation in the same volume, not on its own.

title: Traite des medicaments (Jami al-Mufradat)
shelf_note: Ibn al-Baytar's pharmacopoeia, a major Arabic medical-botanical work; belongs on an Arabic science shelf.
structure_note: Broken structure: 570 page records against pages_count 379. The manuscript appears to be held twice: an older set of unsplit two-page spreads under archived/ with negative page numbers (page -168 shows folios 161/162 as one spread) and a newer set of single leaves under pages/. 183 printed-number repeats and 161 backsteps are consistent with the double set. Negative page numbers are a structural defect in themselves (I2/I3).

book_verdict: An important manuscript of Ibn al-Baytar, but the OCR on all four pages is largely confabulated and the English is fluent nonsense that invents or inverts remedies. The record holds two image sets, one as unsplit spreads with negative page numbers.
reader_summary: This is a Maghribi-hand manuscript of Ibn al-Baytar's Jami' al-mufradat, the great Arabic dictionary of simples. The transcription drifts far from the page after the first lines, and the English states invented remedies with confidence ('treats goats, idiocy, and leprosy'; sheep's blood 'more harmful than epilepsy'). Nothing in the English can be trusted; use the images only.

title: Dhikr Rifāʿī; the Javanese title Kitāb pangdikiran. Or. 7618
shelf_note: A Javanese Sufi dhikr manual (Rifa'i, with Shattari/Naqshbandi lines) in Arabic and Pegon; fits an Islamic/Sufi shelf, though the language field 'Arabic' understates the Javanese.
structure_note: 37 page records against pages_count 24; 24 pages with OCR and 19 translated. Some 13 records look like extra or duplicate leaves (possibly bindings or blanks); worth checking. The language field says Arabic, but the procedural sections are in Javanese (Pegon).

book_verdict: A rare Javanese-Arabic Rifa'i dhikr manual. The Arabic litany pages read well. The Javanese procedural pages are only partly understood, and the English drops or garbles the ritual instructions (fasting, rak'ah counts, petitions).
reader_summary: This is a nineteenth-century Javanese dhikr manual of the Rifa'iyya, opening with an Arabic tawassul to the founders of the Sufi orders and giving ritual instructions in Javanese written in Arabic script. The Arabic lists of saints are transcribed and translated well, apart from small slips such as merging al-Badawi and al-Rifa'i. The Javanese instructions are not reliably translated: they should be flagged as provisional.

title: Kifāyat al-Mabādiʾ ʿalá ʿAqīdah al-Mubtadiʾ Or. 7074
shelf_note: An Ash'ari creed ('aqida) text in the Sanusi tradition; fits the Arabic/Islamic shelf.
structure_note: 18 records, each an unsplit two-page spread, although the OCR claims a split at 500 (I3). Reading order inside a spread is inconsistent: on pages 6 and 10 the left leaf (later page, 23/31) is transcribed before the right leaf (22/30), so the text runs backwards; on page 14 the order is correct. The cover label reads 'Ar. 2887', not Or. 7074; this may be an older shelfmark, low confidence. The author attribution to Taftazani (d. 1390) is doubtful: the text cites al-Sanusi's al-Sughra (Sanusi died c. 1490), so this cannot be Taftazani's own composition (I7).

book_verdict: A clean, legible Naskh creed manuscript whose transcription is mostly good, but the page 10 spread inverts al-Sanusi's position on the ahwal and gives the wrong count of attributes. Spreads are unsplit and sometimes read in the wrong order, and the Taftazani attribution looks wrong.
reader_summary: This is a commentary on an Ash'ari creed in the line of al-Sanusi's al-Sughra, on the divine attributes, prophecy and eschatology. Its attribution to Taftazani cannot be right, since it cites Sanusi. The transcription is of the right text and largely accurate, and the English reads well, but in the technical passages on ahwal and i'tibarat it reverses a position and miscounts the attributes. Within some spreads the left page is read before the right.
